**Explanation:**
The writer effectively uses summary and exposition in the opening paragraphs to compress six weeks of the characters' residency, establish their backgrounds (a choreographer and a marine biologist), and explain the temporary nature of their relationship. Once the necessary context is set, the narrative smoothly transitions into dramatized, real-time scenes—such as the moment they realize the tide has trapped them, their conversation in the rising water while sitting in the kayak, and their final goodbye in the car. Summary is also used skillfully between these key scenes to bridge time (such as the water receding and the hour-and-a-half drive back), maintaining a strong pace while ensuring the emotional climax unfolds in vivid detail through dialogue and action.
